knowledge:
- key_parameters: SNPs=Vector of SNP names ;; studies=Vector of study names ;; beta=Matrix of estimated log-odds ratios ;; sigma=Matrix of standard errors ;; case=Matrix of case counts ;; control=Matrix of control counts ;; meta=Logical flag to compute standard meta-analysis ;; zmax.args=List of arguments for subset search (e.g., custom subset function) ;; pval.args=List of arguments for p-value computation ;; data=Data frame containing individual-level data ;; response.var=Name of response variable (e.g., "TYPE") ;; snp.vars=Vector of SNP variable names ;; adj.vars=Vector of adjustment covariate names ;; types.lab=Vector of disease subtype labels ;; control.lab=Label for control group ;; logit=Logical flag to run overall logistic regression
- alternatives: None mentioned in the provided documentation
- when_to_use: When pooling association signals across multiple studies or traits where true effects may exist only in a subset of studies/traits or in opposite directions, or when analyzing individual-level case-control data with distinct disease subtypes.
- pitfalls: Missing values (NA) can occur in 2-sided subset results (e.g., OR, CI) if estimated betas are all positive or all negative for a SNP. Deprecation warnings may occur when passing character vectors of length > 1 to formula-based functions internally in h.types.

workflows.name: meta_analysis_heterogeneous_traits
workflows.intent: Perform subset-based meta-analysis of summary-level association statistics across multiple studies or traits.
input: vdata.rda (R data file containing study data frames with SNP genotypes, age, and case-control status)
workflows.stages: 1. Load summary data and calculate betas, standard errors (sigmas), case counts, and control counts from individual studies ;; 2. Run subset-based meta-analysis using h.traits ;; 3. Define a custom subset search function and run h.traits with restricted subset search ;; 4. Summarize results using h.summary
workflows.code:
datafile <- system.file("sampleData", "vdata.rda", package="ASSET")
load(datafile)
SNPs    <- paste("SNP", 1:3, sep="")
nSNP    <- length(SNPs)
studies <- paste("STUDY", 1:4, sep="") 
nStudy  <- length(studies)
case    <- matrix(data=NA, nrow=nSNP, ncol=nStudy) 
control <- matrix(data=NA, nrow=nSNP, ncol=nStudy) 
for (i in 1:nStudy) {
  data <- eval(parse(text=paste("data", i, sep="")))
  caseVec <- data[, "CC"] == 1
  controlVec <- !caseVec
  for (j in 1:nSNP) {
    temp <- !is.na(data[, SNPs[j]])
    case[j, i] <- sum(caseVec & temp, na.rm=TRUE)
    control[j, i] <- sum(controlVec & temp, na.rm=TRUE)
  }
}
beta  <- matrix(data=NA, nrow=nSNP, ncol=nStudy) 
sigma <- matrix(data=NA, nrow=nSNP, ncol=nStudy) 
for (i in 1:nStudy) {
  data <- eval(parse(text=paste("data", i, sep="")))
  for (j in 1:nSNP) {
    data[, "SNP"] <- data[, SNPs[j]]
    fit <- glm(CC ~ AGE + SNP, data=data, family=binomial())
    coef <- summary(fit)$coefficients
    beta[j, i] <- coef["SNP", 1]
    sigma[j, i] <- coef["SNP", 2]
  }
}
res <- h.traits(SNPs, studies, beta, sigma, case, control, meta=TRUE)
h.summary(res)
sub.def <- function(logicalVec) {
  sum <- sum(logicalVec)  
  ret <- all(logicalVec[1:sum])
  ret
}
res <- h.traits(SNPs, studies, beta, sigma, case, control, meta=TRUE, 
         zmax.args=list(sub.def=sub.def), pval.args=list(sub.def=sub.def))
h.summary(res)

workflows.name: disease_subtype_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze association of SNPs with distinct disease subtypes using individual-level case-control data.
input: vdata.rda (R data file containing individual-level data frames for multiple studies)
workflows.stages: 1. Combine individual study data frames into a single data frame ;; 2. Create study indicator dummy variables for covariate adjustment ;; 3. Define SNP variables, adjustment variables, and disease subtype labels ;; 4. Run subtype analysis using h.types with logit=TRUE ;; 5. Summarize results using h.summary
workflows.code:
data <- NULL
for (i in 1:nStudy) {
  temp <- eval(parse(text=paste("data", i, sep="")))
  temp[, "STUDY"]  <- i
  data <- rbind(data, temp)
}
for (i in 1:nStudy) {
  dvar <- paste("STUDY_", i, sep="")
  data[, dvar] <- as.numeric(data[, "STUDY"] %in% i)
}
snp.vars <- paste("SNP", 1:3, sep="")
adj.vars <- c("AGE", "STUDY_1", "STUDY_2", "STUDY_3")
types.lab <- paste("TYPE_", 1:3, sep="")
ret <- h.types(data, "TYPE", snp.vars, adj.vars, types.lab, "CONTROL",
               logit=TRUE)
h.summary(ret)
